title: UAV Hyperspectral Mapping of Soil Organic Carbon: A Quality-Controlled Workflow from Field Sampling to Spatial Prediction
content: Retrieval of soil organic carbon (SOC) from uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) hyperspectral imagery depends on how laboratory measurements are linked to pixels at centimetre resolution. This study presents a quality-controlled workflow in which radiometric calibration, harmonisation against proximal spectroradiometer measurements, pixel-level screening, spectral support definition and model validation are treated as interdependent components of a single procedure. Imagery was acquired with a tunable Fabry–Pérot interferometer camera in six bands between 670 and 1100~nm over eight bare soil fields in Flanders, Belgium (85 topsoil samples) and five fields in Central Macedonia, Greece (42 samples). Single pixel spectra, neighbourhood aggregation and local pixel augmentation were compared at radii of 0.25, 0.50 and 1.00~m using Random Forest, XGBoost, a 1D convolutional neural network and TabPFN, with all pixels from a given sampling location assigned to the same cross-validation fold. In Flanders, 23 of 24 neighbourhood configurations reduced RMSE relative to single pixel extraction, the best reaching $R^2 = 0.784$ and RMSE =0.155% SOC. In Central Macedonia, adverse acquisition conditions and a narrow target range prevented a usable SOC model, although electrical conductivity, CaCO3 and pH reached $R^2$ between 0.61 and 0.69. These results indicate that the spectral support should be defined to match the field sampling support, and that this correspondence belongs alongside radiometric calibration, pixel screening and validation in a reproducible workflow for field-scale soil mapping.
